behavioral_notes.observation: Work entries are NOT entered by hand; they are generated per hr.version (the contract snapshot) from the resource.calendar working schedule. _get_version_work_entries_values calls resource.calendar._attendance_intervals_batch to get the weekly attendance intervals, fetches resource.calendar.leaves via _get_leave_domain (global resource_id=False company closures + resource-specific leaves), then computes real_attendances = attendances - leaves - worked_leaves and real_leaves = attendances & leaves. Each interval becomes a dict (date_start/date_stop in employee tz -> UTC) tagged with a work.entry.type, then _generate_work_entries_postprocess splits intervals across local-midnight boundaries, converts date_start/date_stop into a date + float duration, and merges same-day/same-type rows. Generation is bounded by version.date_generated_from/date_generated_to (a high-water mark per version) so a month is never regenerated blindly; contract_date_start gates the range. This whole control flow over resource intervals is invisible in field/relation metadata.

behavioral_notes.element: hr.work.entry.type (attendance / leave / overtime classification + payroll code & rate)
behavioral_notes.observation: A work.entry.type carries a payroll 'code' (required, e.g. WORK100 Attendance, LEAVE120 Paid Time Off, OVERTIME Overtime Hours, LEAVE90 Unpaid), an 'amount_rate' (pay multiplier, default 1.0; 200% = double pay) and the booleans is_leave / is_work (mutually-inverse via _compute_is_work/_inverse_is_work) plus is_extra_hours ('Added to Monthly Pay'). resource.calendar.attendance and resource.calendar.leaves both gain a work_entry_type_id Many2one, so the schedule grid and each leave declare which type the generated entry inherits (default types are xml data records work_entry_type_attendance / work_entry_type_overtime / work_entry_type_leave, resolved by ormcache _get_default_work_entry_type_id). _check_code_unicity enforces code uniqueness per country and the attendance type's country cannot be changed once used. These rate/code semantics are exactly what downstream payroll consumes and are not derivable from metadata.

Every create/write/unlink runs conflict checking inside the _error_checking context manager. _mark_conflicting_work_entries runs a raw SQL aggregate that flags state='conflict' for any (employee, day) whose summed duration is <=0 or >24h; _mark_leaves_outside_schedule re-derives the calendar's _attendance_intervals_batch and flags leave entries falling entirely outside the theoretical schedule; _mark_already_validated_days flags entries colliding with an already-validated day; undefined-type entries are flagged too. action_validate refuses to move entries to state='validated' ('In Payslip') if any conflict exists, and validated entries cannot be deleted (_unlink_except_validated_work_entries) — this is the gate that protects payroll integrity. The stored 'conflict' field surfaces conflicting rows first in the UI. None of this validation logic appears in metadata.

behavioral_notes.element: regeneration on contract/leave/calendar change (hr.version.write + regeneration wizard + cron)
behavioral_notes.observation: hr.version.write reacts to data changes: editing contract_date_start/contract_date_end/date_version calls _remove_work_entries (drops non-validated entries now outside the contract window and rewinds date_generated_from/to); changing resource_calendar_id or work_entry_source (_get_fields_that_recompute_we) triggers _recompute_work_entries, which spawns an hr.work.entry.regeneration.wizard and calls regenerate_work_entries(force=True) for the affected window. The wizard (manager-only) lets a user re-generate a date range for selected employees but EXCLUDES employees with validated entries in that range (validated_work_entry_employee_ids). A monthly cron _cron_generate_missing_work_entries batches (BATCH_SIZE=100, single-company per pass, self-retriggering) the current month's missing entries for all versions with open generated-date gaps. So a contract amendment or an approved leave silently rewrites the affected work entries — a key side-effect metadata cannot reveal.

12 JS files, 10 XML templates, 1 OWL component (WorkEntryType — the colored work-entry-type chip), 4 registry adds (fields:many2one_work_entry_type, fields:work_entry_source_field, fields:many2many_avatar_employee_class, and a dedicated views:work_entries_calendar calendar renderer), 0 patches. Services used: color, display_code, employee_id, resource_calendar_id. Asset bundles: web.assets_backend, web.assets_unit_tests. The UI is a thin colored calendar/list editor over generated entries (no external client app), consistent with work entries being a backend payroll-prep ledger.

resource.calendar.attendance -inherit-> hr.work.entry.type (work_entry_type_id: schedule grid declares the type)

classification.rationale: hr_work_entry is a support activity of Porter's value chain (Stabell & Fjeldstad: a support value configuration, not a primary chain/shop/network flow): it is the payroll-prep time-tracking backbone that converts the resource.calendar working schedule and resource.calendar.leaves time off into a typed, conflict-checked, validatable ledger of payable time (hr.work.entry) per contract version. It builds directly on the 'resource' module (same value_model 'support', same APQC 7.0): it inherits resource.calendar / resource.calendar.attendance / resource.calendar.leaves to attach a work_entry_type_id and calls resource.calendar._attendance_intervals_batch as its generation substrate, then it bridges that working-time into payroll by tagging every interval with a payroll code and rate and gating it through a 'validated' ('In Payslip') state. It does not itself convert demand into a delivered product or run payroll; it sits between scheduling (resource) and payroll, which is exactly APQC PCF 7.0 Develop and Manage Human Capital (manage employee time, attendance and the inputs to compensation) — the same category as its hr parent and the resource module it extends. It is NOT 9.0 Manage Financial Resources (it prepares payroll inputs but performs no accounting) and NOT a primary value flow.

standard_capabilities: automatic work-entry generation per contract version from the resource.calendar working schedule (attendances minus time off)
work-entry types with payroll code, pay rate (amount_rate) and attendance/leave/overtime/extra-hours flags
conflict detection (>24h/day, leaves outside schedule, already-validated collisions) with a 'conflict' state surfaced first
validation lifecycle (draft -> conflict -> validated 'In Payslip' -> cancelled) with validated-entry immutability
regeneration wizard + automatic recompute on contract/calendar/source change, excluding validated periods
monthly cron that fills missing work entries for the current period in batches
calendar/list/pivot views over generated entries, colored by work-entry type
typical_fits: salaried employees on a fixed working schedule (work_entry_source='calendar') generating standard attendance entries each month
public holidays (global resource.calendar.leaves) and approved time off automatically producing leave entries of the right type
country-specific payroll codes/rates mapped onto work-entry types feeding a localized payroll
two-tier HR security (officer reviews, manager owns types & regeneration) with multi-company scoping
common_gaps: attendance-clock-based or planning-based generation (work_entry_source 'attendances'/'planning') requires the hr_attendance / planning bridge apps
linking time-off requests to work entries and global-vs-personal leave precedence requires hr_work_entry_holidays
actual payslip computation / salary rules consume work entries but live in hr_payroll, not here
overtime rules, public-holiday premiums and worked-leave compensation beyond the generic type/rate need localization or custom config
